tasks.title: Composer starts centred and remembers where you drag it
tasks.change: JOE'S SEAT CALL: 'every time I open Synapse I have to reach in and resize the centre bar so it is equidistant between the prompt and the chat. Make equidistant the default, keep the bar for manual resize.' ROOT CAUSE: the composer (_DsInput.__init__, synapse_panel.py ~line 116) hardcodes self._user_h = 132 with self.setFixedHeight(self._user_h). 132 is a constant, so in a tall pane the divider always lands well above centre and the artist re-drags it every session. TWO PARTS, BOTH REQUIRED. (1) START CENTRED: replace the constant first-run height with one computed from the actual available height so the chat area and the composer start equal -- roughly half the space the two of them share, measured at the point the panel knows its own size (a resizeEvent or showEvent, not __init__, where the height is not yet known). CLAMP IT with the values already defined right there: never below self._floor (64) and never above self._max_h (600), so a short pane degrades gracefully instead of producing a composer with no room to type. Keep the existing auto-grow-to-fit-content behaviour and keep _InputResizeGrip working exactly as it does -- the artist must still be able to drag the bar. (2) REMEMBER IT: centred is only the FIRST-RUN answer. When the artist drags the grip, persist the resulting height and restore it on the next launch, so the panel keeps THEIR answer rather than re-imposing ours. Add one key to the settings schema in settings.py -- follow the existing schema-v2 conventions exactly: bump the schema version, extend the documented schema block at the top of the file, add the key to the defaults, and add a migration so files written by the current version load without the key and simply fall back to centred. save_settings is already atomic and best-effort and load_settings already returns defaults on a missing/corrupt/unshaped file and never raises -- preserve both properties; a settings failure must never block boot or lose the artist's session. Persist on drag-release, not on every mouse-move. THIS IS L6, NOT L5: the panel notifies and remembers, it never decides for the artist -- it must never move the divider on its own after first run, and it must never override a height the artist has set. Not profile-conditional: the same behaviour in curious, expert and ml, and no [prominence] or [density] rule may be touched. Add tests/test_rope_composer_height.py: assert the first-run height is computed from available height rather than the 132 constant, assert it clamps to the floor in a short pane and to the max in a very tall one, assert a persisted height is restored in preference to the centred default, and assert a settings file lacking the new key loads cleanly and falls back to centred. Add one line to docs/PROFILES.md under 'Derived design decisions' in the form 'X derived from Y because Z'.

accept.note: SEAT: fresh panel opens with the divider centred; drag it, reopen, it stays where you left it

tasks.title: Connect/Corpus read as buttons in every profile -- and the v5.42.0 claim is corrected
tasks.change: JOE'S RULING, and it deliberately retires a constraint. THE DEFECT: connect and corpus are built as c.Button('Connect', variant='ghost') and c.Button('Corpus', variant='ghost') (synapse_panel.py ~lines 664 and 673). Ghost is transparent, borderless, text-only. On curious they now carry a hero fill so they read as actions; on expert and ml they render as bare text with no button chrome at all, so a new artist has no way to know they are clickable. That is an affordance failure, not a profile distinction. THE FIX: change BOTH from variant='ghost' to variant='secondary' so their STANDARD state is a visible, outlined, unaccented button in every profile. Do not change their labels, their order, their placement, their click wiring, their state gating, or their size. Hero must keep working exactly as it does: on curious the manifest still sends them hero and the existing [prominence="hero"] rules must still fill them with SIGNAL_DEEP knockout over this new secondary base -- verify the cascade still resolves that way and adjust ONLY if the hero rule no longer wins, never by weakening hero. WHAT THIS RETIRES, STATED PLAINLY: L5-5 pinned expert to 'v5.42.0 exactly' and this changes expert's appearance. That pin was scaffolding to stop agent drift during the profile build; the build is done and Joe has ruled. The pin's CAPABILITY guarantee is untouched and remains absolute -- expert still shows every widget at standard prominence with no overlay and no added narration, and every profile still exposes an identical agent capability set. But any claim of PIXEL identity is now false and must not survive this commit. Search docs/PROFILES.md and README.md for every statement that expert is identical to, exactly, or unchanged from v5.42.0 and rewrite each one truthfully: expert is the panel as it ships, every widget at standard prominence, no overlay, no added narration -- identical to v5.42.0 in capability and layout, with the single deliberate change that connect and corpus render as buttons rather than bare text so their affordance is visible. Do not delete the pin's capability language and do not overstate the change. If any test asserts pixel or style identity for expert (as opposed to widget set, order, or capability), update it to assert the capability invariant instead and comment why. Extend tests/test_rope_prominence_visible.py: assert neither connect nor corpus is constructed as ghost, and assert a hero rule still fills them with SIGNAL_DEEP and TEXT_ON_ACCENT. Add one line to docs/PROFILES.md under 'Derived design decisions' in the form 'X derived from Y because Z'.
